Why was this particular individual selected over other candidates, and was there a transparent, competitive selection process?

articles.title: Ebola: Swiss government says Nigeria’s patient likely contracted virus in Uganda
articles.summary:
However, the World Health Organisation (WHO) and the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) said they had not received verified information that the woman travelled to the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), where the current Ebola outbreak began.
The post Ebola: Swiss government says Nigeria’s patient likely contracted virus in Uganda appeared first on Premium Times Ni
articles.hausa_translation: Ebola: Gwamnatin Swiss ta ce majiyyar Nigeria zai iya samun cutin jiya a Uganda
critical_questions: Why does the Swiss government claim knowledge of the patient's travel history while WHO and Africa CDC state they lack verified information?
What is the source and chain of custody for the Swiss government's epidemiological data about this case?
Why is there a discrepancy between official health organizations' findings and the Swiss government's assertion, and who benefits from each narrative?
Has the patient or her contacts been directly interviewed to confirm Uganda travel, or is this based on indirect intelligence?
Why is Nigeria's case being traced to Uganda rather than DRC when the current outbreak originated in DRC according to health authorities?

articles.title: Arokodare joins Osimhen, Dessers, Ndidi on scoresheet as Nigerians shine in Europe

The post Arokodare joins Osimhen, Dessers, Ndidi on scoresheet as Nigerians shine in Europe appeared first on Premium Times Nigeria.
articles.hausa_translation: Victor Osimhen, Cyriel Dessers, Wilfred Ndidi da Tolu Arokodare suka yi ƙwallo ga ƙungiyoyin su, while Ademola Lookman ya ba da taimako kamar yadda 'yan wasan Nigeria suka nuna mahimmanci a gasar ƙungiyoyi masu girma a Gida.
critical_questions: Why does this article focus exclusively on individual player achievements rather than team performance or strategic significance of these matches?
Are these performances being selectively highlighted to boost national pride, and does this reflect actual competitive quality or media bias toward Nigerian players?
What is the timeline and context of these matches—are they from the same matchday, and does grouping them together create a misleading impression of momentum?
Who benefits from this framing (Nigerian media, player agents, advertisers) and does it serve editorial interest over comprehensive sports reporting?

articles.title: Three sentenced to death for kidnapping Catholic priests
articles.summary:
Taledo Demiel, Namomai Medan and Mikaila Yusuf were convicted over the abduction of Reverend Fathers Matthew Dutsemi and Abraham Sauman.
The post Three sentenced to death for kidnapping Catholic priests appeared first on Premium Times Nigeria.
articles.hausa_translation: Mutum uku an yanke musu hukuncin morte saboda zoben masu godiya na Katolika. Taledo Demiel, Namomai Medan da Mikaila Yusuf an gida su don zoben Reverend Fathers Matthew Dutsemi da Abraham Sauman.
critical_questions: What were the specific circumstances and evidence presented that led to these death sentences, and was due process followed?
Why were Catholic priests specifically targeted, and does this reflect broader religious tensions or organized criminal networks in the region?
What is the track record of Nigerian courts in death penalty cases regarding appeals, commutations, and actual executions?
Were the three defendants represented by adequate legal counsel, and what are the details of their confessions or evidence?
How does this case connect to the wider kidnapping crisis affecting religious leaders in Nigeria, and what preventive measures are being implemented?

articles.title: Lagos: One dead, several feared trapped as building collapses
articles.summary: One person has been confirmed dead, while three adult males have been rescued following the collapse of a two-storey building under construction in the Fadeyi area of Lagos State. Several other persons are feared trapped beneath the rubble as emergency responders continue search and rescue operations at the scene. The Lagos State Emergency Management Agency […]
articles.hausa_translation: Lagos: Mutum daya ya mutu, mutane da yawa ana tsamanin sun kama jiya a cikin rufaffiyar gida. Mutum daya an tabbatar da mutuwarsa, har ma'aikatan neman jiya sun cire maza uku a jikin rufaffiyar gida mai baje-baje na gida gida a yankin Fadeyi na jihar Lagos. Mutane da yawa ana tsamanin sun kama karkashin tarkace-tarkacen gida yayin da masu gaggawa ke tafiya yin neman jiya.
critical_questions: What were the building safety and structural inspections supposed to be in place before construction, and who was responsible for oversight?
Has there been a pattern of building collapses in Fadeyi or Lagos more broadly, and what enforcement gaps exist in construction regulation?
Why was a two-storey building under construction in this area—who owns/developed it and what permits were issued?
How quickly did emergency responders arrive, and are there adequate rescue resources being deployed compared to the scale of the incident?
What accounts for the gap between persons feared trapped versus confirmed rescued—how many individuals were actually on-site and is there accountability tracking for workers?

articles.title: APC accuses Atiku of politicising ebola response, says N10bn untouched
articles.summary: The All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council has accused former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar of politicising Nigeria’s Ebola response, insisting that approved emergency funds remain untouched. The council’s spokesperson, Mr Dele Alake, said this in a statement issued on Thursday in Abuja. Daily Trust reports that President Bola Tinubu approved N10 billion for the Ebola [&#823
articles.hausa_translation: APC ta zargi Atiku da yin siyasar jiya da jiya akan amfani da Ebola, ta ce N10 miljari ba a taɓa tuɓi ba
critical_questions: Why is N10 billion approved but reportedly untouched - what are the stated reasons and who can verify the fund status independently?
What specific statements from Atiku constitute 'politicising Ebola response' and is this characterization or substantive critique?
Who benefits politically from this accusation being made now, and what alternative narratives exist about Ebola preparedness spending?
Are there documented cases of actual Ebola response delays or mismanagement that prompted Atiku's comments, or is this purely political timing?
Why is the APC campaign council (not health officials) making this statement, and what is the source of their fund status knowledge?

articles.title: Family: Fasoranti to be buried December 17
articles.summary: The family of the late leader of Afenifere, Pa Reuben Famuyide Fasoranti, has announced that the elder statesman will be buried on December 17, 2026. The burial arrangements were contained in a programme of activities signed by his son, Dr. Taiwo Fasoranti, who is also the Secretary to the Ondo State Government. The family described […]
articles.hausa_translation: Dangi: Za a binne Fasoranti a Disamba 17
critical_questions: Why is the burial scheduled nearly two years in the future (December 2026) rather than within customary timeframes, and what are the financial/political implications?
Who benefits from controlling the narrative around this prominent Afenifere leader's burial - are there succession power struggles within the organization being obscured?
Why is the Secretary to Ondo State Government (his son) the primary spokesperson rather than Afenifere leadership, and does this conflate state power with family/ethnic authority?
What funeral expenses and resource mobilization are being planned, and which political figures/donors will gain visibility through association with this event?
Are there competing claims or disagreements about burial arrangements that the 'family announcement' framing might be suppressing?

articles.title: Uproar in Rivers over forced virginity test on female students
articles.summary: There is tension at Government Comprehensive High School (SNR), Taabaa, Khana Local Government Area of Rivers State, over allegations that a monarch subjected female students to forced virginity tests. The management of the school has kicked against such an act, saying it contravened the dignity of the girl child. The management staff of the school […]
articles.hausa_translation: Rikicin a Rivers kan tilastawa da jiya ta matan dalibai - Wani sarki ya tilasta da karfi matan dalibai na sakandare don binciken virginity. Wajen makaranta ya ki aiki kamar haka cewa ba ya dace da mutuncin yarinya.
critical_questions: What is the specific authority and jurisdiction of the monarch to conduct such tests, and who authorized or enabled this action?
What evidence exists of these tests occurring, and have survivors been interviewed independently or only through school management accounts?
Why does the school management's opposition appear only after allegations surfaced rather than during the alleged incidents?
Are there other documented cases of similar practices at this or other institutions in the region that suggest a pattern?
What accountability mechanisms or legal actions are being pursued against the monarch, and what political or social factors might shield or expose him?
